why_how.text: On the passing lane of a multilane road, move right for faster traffic approaching from behind, regardless of your own speed, unless a stated exception applies.
The passing-lane move-right rule allows exceptions when traffic, weather, an obstruction or another hazard makes staying in that lane necessary.
Staying in the passing lane may be necessary to comply with a law or traffic-control device, to leave the road or turn left, or to pay a toll or use a toll pass.
Authorized emergency vehicles on official duty and vehicles performing highway construction or maintenance are exceptions to the described passing-lane move-right rule.

To center the vehicle after reversing into the parallel space, select drive, steer right and pull forward carefully.
Use the proper turn signal before parallel parking and again before leaving the space.

For a bus or other large vehicle, use all mirrors and a reliable person to observe and direct the backing maneuver.

why_how.text: The handbook's Super Speeder threshold is a speeding conviction at seventy-five miles per hour or more on a two-lane road, or at eighty-five miles per hour or more on any Georgia road.

The handbook describes a separate two hundred-dollar state Super Speeder charge in addition to local fines. Late payment results in license suspension and an additional fifty-dollar reinstatement charge.
Unless a different limit is posted, the handbook's general maximum in an urban or residential district is thirty miles per hour.
For an unpaved county road, the handbook's default maximum is thirty-five miles per hour unless posted otherwise.
The handbook's general rural-interstate maximum is seventy miles per hour, subject to the posted limit.
On an urban interstate or a multilane divided highway, the handbook gives a general maximum of sixty-five miles per hour unless another limit is posted.

why_how.text: For other areas, the handbook's general maximum is fifty-five miles per hour unless posted otherwise.
Road authorities can adjust limits for local conditions temporarily or permanently. Watch signs, including temporary school or construction-zone limits, and reduce speed before entering the zone.
Do not drive so slowly that normal, reasonable traffic is impeded, except when the lower speed is needed to operate safely.
Where several lanes carry traffic in the same direction, slower traffic should stay right except to pass or turn left. Do not remain in the passing lane while a faster vehicle overtakes from behind.
Some highways have posted minimum speeds. If unable to meet the minimum, choose another route.

At a railroad crossing, stop between fifteen and fifty feet from the closest rail when warning lights flash, a gate is down, a flagger signals a stop, a posted stop sign requires it, or an approaching train presents an immediate hazard.

why_how.text: Never drive around, under or through a lowered railroad gate.
After stopping for a train, wait until every track is clear, warning lights have stopped, gates are raised and crossing is safe.
Approach tracks cautiously, prepare to stop, look and listen in both directions, then check again before crossing.
Do not enter a railroad crossing without enough room to drive completely through it without stopping. Once safely committed, keep moving across the tracks.
If the vehicle stalls on tracks, leave it immediately and move away. Find the emergency-notification sign and call for help, explaining that a vehicle is on the tracks.
